title: 9,000 BTU vs 12,000 BTU Mini Split: Sq Ft, Amps & Short-Cycling Risk
shortLabel: 9,000 BTU vs 12,000 BTU Mini Split
summary: Use 9,000 BTU for 150–400 sq ft bedrooms/offices to prevent humidity short-cycling; step up to 12,000 BTU for 400–550 sq ft rooms or uninsulated spaces.

title: 12,000 BTU vs 18,000 BTU Mini Split: 1-Ton vs 1.5-Ton Comparison
shortLabel: 12,000 BTU vs 18,000 BTU Mini Split
summary: 12,000 BTU often runs on 115V (15A–20A) and covers up to 550 sq ft; 18,000 BTU requires 208/230V (20A double-pole) and handles 600–900 sq ft or 2-car garages.

title: 18,000 BTU vs 24,000 BTU Mini Split: 2-Car Garage & Great Room Sizing
shortLabel: 18,000 BTU vs 24,000 BTU Mini Split
summary: 18,000 BTU (1.5-Ton) fits insulated 600–850 sq ft spaces on 12 AWG wire; 24,000 BTU (2-Ton) requires 10 AWG wire / 25A–30A breaker and cools up to 1,200 sq ft.

title: 24,000 BTU vs 36,000 BTU Mini Split: 2-Ton vs 3-Ton Workshop & Barn Guide
shortLabel: 24,000 BTU vs 36,000 BTU Mini Split
summary: 24,000 BTU covers ~1,000–1,200 sq ft; 36,000 BTU (3-Ton) handles 1,400–1,800 sq ft pole barns or 3–4 zone homes on an 8 AWG / 35A–40A 230V circuit.

title: 115V vs 230V Mini Split: Efficiency, Breaker Size & Cold-Weather Performance
shortLabel: 115V vs 230V Mini Split
summary: 230V mini-splits draw half the amperage of 115V units, run cooler on long wire runs, and are standard for hyper-heat cold-climate models above 12,000 BTU.

title: Two Single-Zone Mini Splits vs One Dual-Zone: Cost, SEER2 & Redundancy
shortLabel: Two Single-Zone Mini Splits vs One Dual-Zone
summary: Two 12,000 BTU single-zone units typically deliver 3–5 higher SEER2 points, lower minimum turndown (less short-cycling), and full backup if one condenser fails.

title: 9,000 BTU Mini Split Amps, Breaker Size & Wire Gauge Chart (115V & 230V)
shortLabel: 9,000 BTU Mini Split Amps, Breaker Size & Wire Gauge Chart (115V & 230V)
summary: A 9,000 BTU inverter draws 5–8A running (MCA ~10A–15A), requiring a 15A breaker and 14 AWG or 12 AWG copper wire.

title: 12,000 BTU Mini Split Amps, Breaker Size & Wire Gauge Chart (115V & 230V)
shortLabel: 12,000 BTU Mini Split Amps, Breaker Size & Wire Gauge Chart (115V & 230V)
summary: 12,000 BTU 115V units usually specify a 20A breaker (12 AWG); 230V models typically need a 15A double-pole breaker (14/12 AWG).

title: 18,000 BTU Mini Split Amps, Breaker Size & Wire Gauge Chart (230V)
shortLabel: 18,000 BTU Mini Split Amps, Breaker Size & Wire Gauge Chart (230V)
summary: 18,000 BTU 230V units specify 20A MOP double-pole breaker with 12/2 Romex or #12 THHN in liquid-tight whip to the outdoor disconnect.

title: 24,000 BTU Mini Split Amps, Breaker Size & Wire Gauge Chart (230V)
shortLabel: 24,000 BTU Mini Split Amps, Breaker Size & Wire Gauge Chart (230V)
summary: 24,000 BTU condensers require a 25A or 30A double-pole 230V breaker and 10 AWG copper conductors (verify nameplate MCA & MOP).

title: 36,000 BTU Mini Split Amps, Breaker Size & Wire Gauge Chart (230V)
shortLabel: 36,000 BTU Mini Split Amps, Breaker Size & Wire Gauge Chart (230V)
summary: 36,000 BTU (3-Ton) condensers typically require a 35A or 40A double-pole 230V breaker with 8 AWG copper conductors.

title: 48,000 BTU Mini Split Amps, Breaker Size & Wire Gauge Chart (230V)
shortLabel: 48,000 BTU Mini Split Amps, Breaker Size & Wire Gauge Chart (230V)
summary: 48,000 BTU (4-Ton) multi-zone condensers specify 45A–50A MOP double-pole breakers using #8 AWG THHN or #6 AWG NM-B.

title: How Much Electricity Does a Mini Split Use Per Month? (9k to 36k BTU Cost)
shortLabel: How Much Electricity Does a Mini Split Use Per Month? (9k to 36k BTU Cost)
summary: Because inverter compressors throttle to 30%–50% load once the room reaches setpoint, a 12k BTU 20 SEER2 unit costs just $18–$32/month to run.

title: Mini Split vs Window AC: Electricity Cost, Noise (19 dB vs 55 dB) & ROI
shortLabel: Mini Split vs Window AC
summary: A 22 SEER2 inverter mini-split cuts cooling electricity use by 40%–55% over a standard 11 CEER window AC while adding heat-pump winter heating.

title: Mini Split Heat Pump vs Electric Baseboard Heat: Winter Bill Savings
shortLabel: Mini Split Heat Pump vs Electric Baseboard Heat
summary: Electric resistance baseboards have a COP of 1.0 (100% efficiency); a cold-climate mini-split achieves COP 2.8–3.8 (280%–380%), cutting winter electric bills by 60%–70%.

title: Mini Split Heat Pump vs Propane Garage Heater: Annual Operating Cost
shortLabel: Mini Split Heat Pump vs Propane Garage Heater
summary: At $2.75/gal propane and $0.15/kWh electricity, a cold-climate mini-split heats a 2-car garage for ~45% less than propane while also providing summer AC.

title: Ductless Mini Split vs Central Air Conditioning: Duct Loss & SEER2 Guide
shortLabel: Ductless Mini Split vs Central Air Conditioning
summary: Traditional attic ductwork loses 20%–30% of conditioned air to leaks and conduction; ductless mini-splits eliminate duct losses completely.

title: 16 SEER2 vs 20 SEER2 vs 25 SEER2 Mini Split: Real Dollar Payback
shortLabel: 16 SEER2 vs 20 SEER2 vs 25 SEER2 Mini Split
summary: Jumping from 16 to 20 SEER2 cuts cooling kWh by 20% with a fast 3–4 year payback; 25+ SEER2 shines brightest in hot Southern climates or off-grid solar.

title: Hyper-Heat (-13°F) vs Standard Mini Split (5°F): Heating Capacity Drop
shortLabel: Hyper-Heat (-13°F) vs Standard Mini Split (5°F)
summary: Standard heat pumps lose 40%–50% of rated BTU below 15°F; vapor-injected Hyper-Heat units deliver 100% rated BTU down to 5°F and 75%+ down to -13°F.

title: Mitsubishi vs Daikin vs Fujitsu Mini Split: Cold-Climate & Turndown Matrix
shortLabel: Mitsubishi vs Daikin vs Fujitsu Mini Split
summary: All three Japanese tier-1 brands deliver 15–20 year lifespans, ultra-low 19 dB sound floors, and strong winter HSPF2 ratings.

title: MRCOOL DIY Pre-Charged vs Pro-Installed Mini Split: Cost & Warranty
shortLabel: MRCOOL DIY Pre-Charged vs Pro-Installed Mini Split
summary: Pre-charged quick-connect linesets save $2,000–$3,500 in HVAC installation labor for garages and workshops, while pro flare installs optimize line length.

title: Wall-Mounted vs 4-Way Ceiling Cassette Mini Split: Airflow & Install Guide
shortLabel: Wall-Mounted vs 4-Way Ceiling Cassette Mini Split
summary: High-wall heads are cheapest and easiest to clean; 1-way and 4-way ceiling cassettes fit cleanly between 16" O.C. joists for flush architectural ceilings.

title: Floor-Console vs Wall-Mounted Mini Split for Attics & Sunrooms
shortLabel: Floor-Console vs Wall-Mounted Mini Split for Attics & Sunrooms
summary: Floor-mounted consoles fit neatly on 36-inch knee walls and under sunroom windows where high-wall clearance does not exist.

title: Concealed Short-Ducted Mini Split Sizing & Static Pressure Guide
shortLabel: Concealed Short-Ducted Mini Split Sizing & Static Pressure Guide
summary: Slim ducted air handlers hide in closets or drop ceilings to serve 2–3 adjacent rooms quietly with traditional supply registers.

title: BTU to Tons HVAC Conversion Chart (6,000 BTU to 60,000 BTU)
shortLabel: BTU to Tons HVAC Conversion Chart (6,000 BTU to 60,000 BTU)
summary: 1 Ton of refrigeration equals exactly 12,000 BTU/hr (0.5 Ton = 6k, 0.75 Ton = 9k, 1 Ton = 12k, 1.5 Ton = 18k, 2 Ton = 24k, 3 Ton = 36k).

title: ACCA Manual J Load Calculation vs 20 BTU/Sq Ft Rule of Thumb
shortLabel: ACCA Manual J Load Calculation vs 20 BTU/Sq Ft Rule of Thumb
summary: The 20 BTU/sq ft rule breaks down in sunrooms, high-ceiling pole barns, and uninsulated garages—ceiling height, insulation R-value, and climate zone must be factored in.

title: Why Oversizing a Mini Split Causes Clammy Rooms & Mold (Turndown Trap)
shortLabel: Why Oversizing a Mini Split Causes Clammy Rooms & Mold (Turndown Trap)
summary: An oversized AC cools the air in 5 minutes before the coil can condense moisture—always check Minimum BTU Turndown capacity on the submittal sheet.

title: Mini Split Dry Mode vs Standalone Dehumidifier: Energy & Humidity
shortLabel: Mini Split Dry Mode vs Standalone Dehumidifier
summary: Dry Mode slows the indoor blower fan to super-chill the coil and pull 2–4 pints/hour of moisture—ideal for humid basements and summer shoulders.

title: Mini Split Line Set Length Limits (Min 10 ft, Max 82–164 ft) & Pre-Charge
shortLabel: Mini Split Line Set Length Limits (Min 10 ft, Max 82–164 ft) & Pre-Charge
summary: Most condensers are pre-charged for 25 ft of lineset; shorter runs under 10 ft cause vibration noise, while longer runs require adding 0.16–0.32 oz/ft of R-410A or R-454B.

title: R-410A vs R-454B vs R-32 Mini Split Refrigerants (2025–2026 EPA Transition)
shortLabel: R-410A vs R-454B vs R-32 Mini Split Refrigerants (2025–2026 EPA Transition)
summary: Low-GWP A2L refrigerants (R-454B and R-32) replace R-410A in new equipment with 5%–8% better heat transfer and similar pressure ratings.

title: What Size Generator or Power Station Runs a Mini Split? (Zero Surge Myth)
shortLabel: What Size Generator or Power Station Runs a Mini Split? (Zero Surge Myth)
summary: Because inverter mini-splits ramp up softly via DC variable-frequency drives, a 12,000 BTU unit has virtually ZERO starting surge and runs on a 2,000W inverter generator.

title: Running a Mini Split on Solar Panels & LiFePO4 Batteries (Off-Grid Math)
shortLabel: Running a Mini Split on Solar Panels & LiFePO4 Batteries (Off-Grid Math)
summary: A 12,000 BTU 22 SEER2 inverter averages 450W–650W after cooldown—easily powered by 1,200W of solar panels and a 5 kWh 48V LiFePO4 battery bank.

title: Mini Split Condensate Drain Gravity Slope vs Mini Pump Sizing
shortLabel: Mini Split Condensate Drain Gravity Slope vs Mini Pump Sizing
summary: Always prioritize gravity drainage (1/4" per foot downward slope) on exterior walls; use an ultra-quiet Aspen/Sauermann condensate pump only for interior walls.

title: Cold-Climate Mini Split Snow Stand Height & Defrost Drainage Clearance
shortLabel: Cold-Climate Mini Split Snow Stand Height & Defrost Drainage Clearance
summary: Elevate outdoor heat pump condensers 12" to 24" above average local snowpack on heavy risers so winter defrost water drains freely without freezing the coil.

title: NEC 440.14 Mini Split Outdoor Disconnect Box & Whip Wiring Requirements
shortLabel: NEC 440.14 Mini Split Outdoor Disconnect Box & Whip Wiring Requirements
summary: NEC 440.14 requires a lockable non-fused or fused disconnect switch within sight of and within 50 feet of the outdoor condenser unit.

title: High Ceiling BTU Multiplier Chart (8 ft vs 10 ft vs 12 ft vs 16 ft)
shortLabel: High Ceiling BTU Multiplier Chart (8 ft vs 10 ft vs 12 ft vs 16 ft)
summary: Every additional 2 feet of ceiling height adds 25% more air volume to condition—a 12-foot ceiling needs ~1.40× to 1.50× the BTU of an 8-foot room.

title: US IECC Climate Zone BTU Multiplier Chart (Zone 1 Miami to Zone 7 Minnesota)
shortLabel: US IECC Climate Zone BTU Multiplier Chart (Zone 1 Miami to Zone 7 Minnesota)
summary: Zone 1–2 hot/humid states size for peak cooling & latent dehumidification; Zone 5–7 northern states size for -5°F to -15°F design heating loads.

title: 6,000 BTU vs 9,000 BTU Mini Split for Small Bedrooms (100–250 Sq Ft)
shortLabel: 6,000 BTU vs 9,000 BTU Mini Split for Small Bedrooms (100–250 Sq Ft)
summary: For tight 120–200 sq ft bedrooms, a 6,000 BTU head prevents temperature overshoot; check minimum modulation BTU before choosing 9,000 BTU.

title: 15,000 BTU vs 18,000 BTU Mini Split: Best Size for 600–750 Sq Ft Rooms
shortLabel: 15,000 BTU vs 18,000 BTU Mini Split
summary: 15,000 BTU bridges the gap between 12k and 18k for 550–700 sq ft living rooms, often offering lower minimum turndown than 18k chassis.

title: 30,000 BTU vs 36,000 BTU Mini Split: 2.5-Ton vs 3-Ton Capacity & Amps
shortLabel: 30,000 BTU vs 36,000 BTU Mini Split
summary: 30,000 BTU fits 30A/10 AWG circuits for ~1,300–1,500 sq ft; 36,000 BTU steps up to 35A–40A/8 AWG for up to 1,800 sq ft or 4-zone layouts.
